basics.name: Cláudio Araújo
basics.title: Mid-level Backend Engineer @ Avanade
basics.valueProp: I move critical systems from legacy to cloud-native without stopping the business that runs on them — reactive Java and Kotlin APIs, hexagonal architecture, and resilience measured in production, not on slides.
basics.summary: Backend Engineer with 3+ years on mission-critical systems in banking and energy. Java 8–21, Kotlin, Spring Boot and Quarkus, focused on reactive APIs, microservices, hexagonal architecture and legacy modernisation.
basics.availability: Open to remote roles — Brazil and Europe

projects.name: MCP Regression Platform
projects.tagline: Regression-readiness platform built on MCP, RAG and a deterministic agent
projects.problem: Before every BFF regression run, someone has to manually check whether dependencies are up, whether contracts still match and whether the environment can take the test suite. It burns hours and fails silently.
projects.description: It answers one operational question — is this environment ready to regress this BFF? — by combining dependency discovery, health checks, contract validation and smoke tests. Exposes 7 Tools, 6 Resources and 4 Prompts over MCP (Streamable HTTP and STDIO), with the LLM confined to interpretation and the workflow kept deterministic. Hexagonal modular monolith, capability-based authorisation on every Tool and Resource, and prompt-injection mitigation at the MCP boundary.

projects.name: ServiceTrack Platform
projects.tagline: Distributed work-order system split across four repositories with clear ownership
projects.problem: Repair shops lose track of every job between paper, spreadsheets and WhatsApp — and customers only find out the quote once the car is already in pieces.
projects.description: Covers the full work-order lifecycle — intake, diagnosis, quoting, customer approval via magic link, execution and handover — with an audit trail over business operations. The split is deliberate: the API owns the domain and the Flyway migrations, CPF authentication lives in an AWS Lambda, RDS has its own repository with a connection budget, and network, EKS, API Gateway and ArgoCD sit in the IaC repository. Decisions recorded in 25 ADRs and 8 RFCs.

projects.name: MockSmith
projects.tagline: Runtime API mock engine driven straight from the OpenAPI contract
projects.problem: Teams sit blocked waiting on the service they depend on — and once it exists, nobody can test how their own application behaves when it goes down, stalls, or returns broken JSON.
projects.description: Reads an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger document and brings up a live HTTP server straight from the contract — no static mock files, no config. Response bodies are generated by priority: contract example, schema example, then format-aware fake data. Chaos profiles roll weighted outcomes across success, documented business errors, 500s, timeouts, malformed JSON and dropped connections, while the Admin API overrides status and latency per endpoint without a restart. The internal version of this tool saves roughly 12 h/week per team.

projects.name: Sellvia API
projects.tagline: Multi-tenant catalogue API with media stored in object storage
projects.problem: Small merchants selling from a catalogue have nowhere to centralise products, categories and photos — so their inventory ends up living in a phone photo album.
projects.description: Kotlin and Spring Boot REST backend for a multi-tenant catalogue: authentication, company administration, products, categories and media upload to Cloudflare R2 through the S3 SDK. Domain isolated by hexagonal architecture with explicit ports and adapters, Flyway migrations and a JUnit + MockK test suite. It serves the Android app of the same platform.

projects.name: HSG Hospital Information System
projects.tagline: Hospital information system in Java EE — a modular monolith packaged as an EAR
projects.problem: Records, scheduling and clinical documents usually live in separate systems that never talk to each other — so patient information arrives incomplete at the point of care.
projects.description: HIS built on Java EE with JSF, EJB and JPA, packaged as an EAR and deployed on WildFly. Authentication and authorisation delegated to Keycloak, clinical documents in MinIO object storage, schema versioned with Flyway and a full environment in Docker Compose. Modularity is internal: each domain is a module with its own boundary inside the monolith, keeping deployment simple without letting the code tangle.

projects.name: ServiceTrack AWS IaC
projects.tagline: ServiceTrack IaC: network, EKS, API Gateway and GitOps across two isolated environments
projects.problem: Standing an environment up by hand gets the order wrong and takes the other environment down with it.
projects.description: Modular Terraform with staging and production separated by their own state and sizing. Provisions VPC, EKS, ECR, ArgoCD, the auth Lambda and external exposure through API Gateway from a versioned OpenAPI contract. Workflows orchestrate the network → database → stack order, and teardown in reverse.

projects.name: ServiceTrack Auth Lambda
projects.tagline: Serverless CPF authentication issuing RS256 JWTs
projects.problem: Keeping login inside the main API ties the authentication lifecycle to the domain's deploy cycle.
projects.description: Quarkus + Kotlin service packaged as an AWS Lambda that validates CPF and password, checks the user and issues RS256-signed JWTs. The domain carries no framework dependency, with value objects for CPF, email and password and explicit inbound and outbound ports.

projects.name: Go Event-Driven Microservices
projects.tagline: Go microservices monorepo wired through a RabbitMQ event bus
projects.problem: Synchronous sign-up couples services: if the notification service goes down, sign-up goes down with it.
projects.description: Event-driven architecture with auth-service, notification-service and user-worker communicating over RabbitMQ. Each service publishes and consumes events without knowing the others, so they scale and fail independently. Tests with gomock and a full Docker Compose environment.

projects.name: Sellvia Android
projects.tagline: Sellvia Android app for managing the catalogue in the field
projects.problem: People selling on the move need to register a product and check a price without opening a laptop.
projects.description: Jetpack Compose Android client consuming the Sellvia REST API. Clean Architecture with MVVM, dependency injection via Koin, Navigation Compose routing and Coil image loading. Covers products, categories, catalogue and company data.

projects.name: EventNtfy API
projects.tagline: Email and SMS notification API with scheduled jobs
projects.problem: Every application reimplements its own email and SMS sending, with credentials scattered across five repositories.
projects.description: A single notification service on Spring Boot: email through Spring Mail and SMS through Twilio, with scheduled jobs for recurring dispatches. CI/CD pipeline on GitHub Actions, Docker packaging and MySQL persistence.

projects.name: LibraryControl
projects.tagline: Plain-Java REST API with no framework, as a fundamentals exercise
projects.problem: Frameworks hide what actually happens between an HTTP request and a row in the database.
projects.description: A book-lending system written without Spring and with as few libraries as possible: HTTP server, manual routing, a generic reflection-based DAO and JWT authentication all implemented by hand. The goal was to understand every layer a framework normally abstracts away.

projects.name: Personal Portfolio
projects.tagline: This site: a trilingual static portfolio on Next.js 14
projects.problem: A portfolio that depends on a CMS or an external API breaks exactly when a recruiter opens the link.
projects.description: App Router with locale routing, flash-free light and dark themes, and content loaded from typed JSON files versioned alongside the code — with no external calls at all. Exported as a static site and published to GitHub Pages through GitHub Actions.

projects.name: TCAteliê E-commerce
projects.tagline: Full-stack e-commerce delivered to a real client, with web and Android admin
projects.problem: An atelier selling only through in-person orders had no digital channel and no order tracking.
projects.description: Storefront, web admin panel and Android app on a Spring Boot backend with Spring Security and JWT. Infrastructure migrated from Azure to AWS over the course of the project, provisioned with Terraform and fronted by NGINX.

experience.summary: Reactive microservices and BFFs for critical banking systems at a multinational Microsoft-partner consultancy.
highlights: Designed and delivered microservices and BFFs in Java 21 and Spring Boot, with reactive APIs on Spring WebFlux and Project Reactor.
Implemented resilience with Resilience4j — retry with exponential backoff and Circuit Breaker — cutting latency under peak load and stopping failures from cascading between services.
Added reactive Redis caching to the BFF and the microservices using advanced commands (JSON.SET, SEARCH), removing redundant calls.
Built an internal Go tool that generates HTTP mocks from OpenAPI contracts, decoupling three teams and saving roughly 12 h/week per team.
Applied Hexagonal Architecture, DDD and Clean Architecture to new features, and ran GitOps environments with ArgoCD.

experience.summary: Mission-critical Java applications for one of the largest clients in the energy sector.
highlights: Implemented parallel processing for bulk data export: reports that already failed at 1 year of history now export 6+ years with no downtime.
Investigated and resolved production incidents on mission-critical systems, bringing recovery MTTR down.
Administered Red Hat OpenShift environments — provisioning, scaling and log analysis.
Acted as technical reference for impact analysis and systemic understanding of the Java 8, JSF and PrimeFaces legacy.

experience.summary: REST APIs for energy-sector data ingestion and legacy modernisation towards microservices.
highlights: Built REST APIs in Java and Spring Boot for data ingestion and processing, serving a high daily request volume.
Built React and TypeScript interfaces for internal data-visualisation dashboards.
Took part in modernising legacy applications (Java 8, JSF, PrimeFaces, EJB) towards a microservices architecture.
Participated in Scrum ceremonies and Sprint Reviews directly with the client.

experience.summary: First production experience: maintaining Java 8 applications and building REST APIs.
highlights: Developed and maintained Java 8 applications and built REST APIs with Spring Boot.
Built React interfaces for internal tooling.
Promoted to Junior Developer within 10 months.
